functions.rationale:
**Function behavior.** `render_cli_detail_page` (src/index.rs ~L439-454) is a thin wrapper. It writes the heading `# \`name\`` and a `Definition: \`source\`` line. It then delegates everything else to `render_detail_sections`, passing the definition text, kind, loaded evidence and render sources. It has no branches or error paths of its own.

**Applicable requirements.** I read the full requirements set (`*`) and the `requirements.cli.*` input.
- `requirements.cli.info` is the requirement that governs this function. It covers CLI output as Markdown with the kind-labeled definition, Validation findings, Rationale and Inputs structure, including readable output for missing or invalid evidence. The only caller is the info command path in src/commands.rs, around L119-127.
- `requirements.index.detail_format` and `requirements.index.invalid_detail` describe the shared detail-page structure. They are cited on `render_detail_sections` (src/index.rs ~L456-458), which actually implements that structure. They are also cited on `render_detail_page` (~L411-413), the mdBook wrapper that builds its own page.
- `requirements.cli.info` itself says the CLI output must match the mdBook detail-page structure. So the CLI wrapper's own obligation is the info requirement, and the detail-format and invalid-detail obligations are discharged in the shared helper that carries those citations.
- The CLI wrapper adds no mdBook-specific behavior: no links, badges or index back-references. So `requirements.index.navigation`, `requirements.index.source_links`, `requirements.index.state` and `requirements.examples.index` do not apply to it.
- `requirements.cli.definition_glob_search` is an example that cites `cli.info` and `cli.status`. The glob matching and ordering happen in the caller, not here.
- The remaining authoring, CI, configuration, definitions, references, setup and integration requirements concern other behavior.

**Conclusion.** The existing `{impl}` citation of `requirements.cli.info` accounts for the wrapper's observable behavior. The shared formatting obligations are cited at the helper that implements them. I found no applicable requirement or example that is missing.

When `habeas add-input` creates or refreshes evidence, it MUST also capture or refresh the definition inputs required by the resulting record, including dependencies of its subject text and all reviewed inputs.

Repeated references MUST NOT create duplicate definition inputs. Any change to the record MUST leave its determination false pending reassessment. If no inputs or other record contents change, the record MUST remain unchanged.

An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.

Requirement and example evidence MUST include a definition input for every term referenced by its subject text or reviewed inputs. Rust function attestations MUST include definition inputs for every term referenced by their reviewed inputs, including selected requirements and examples.

Habeas MUST repeatedly include definitions referenced by required definitions until the set reaches a fixed point. Each required definition MUST have exactly one definition input per evidence record. Cyclic references MUST be permitted and MUST NOT cause repeated expansion or nontermination.
Validation MUST report missing required definition inputs and MUST NOT silently refresh snapshots.

A requirements input selects `requirements.cli.*`. A selected requirement references `glossary.command`, which is captured as a separate definition input despite not matching that glob. An unreferenced definition named `requirements.cli.unrelated` is not selected merely because its name matches the glob. {cite}`requirements.definitions.selection`

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.

A definition named `glossary.first_parent_history` declares the phrase "first-parent history". A term reference to that name renders the phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to the declaration, without displaying the identifier or a badge. {cite}`requirements.definitions.references`

An evidence record has determination true and a current definition input. After the definition changes, validation reports stale evidence without modifying the record. Running `habeas add-input` for that record refreshes its required definition input and leaves determination false pending review. {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` {cite}`requirements.definitions.capture`

The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.

Existing requirements input globs MUST continue to select requirements and named examples, excluding named definitions. Definitions referenced by selected texts MUST be captured as separate definition inputs, regardless of whether their names match the glob. Sharing a glob's matching name prefix alone MUST NOT make a definition a dependency.

Requirement R references definition A. A references B, and B references A. R's evidence contains one definition input for A and one for B. A function attestation whose requirements input selects R also requires both inputs. Dependency collection terminates. Changing B's phrase or body invalidates both records' snapshots of B. {cite}`requirements.definitions.dependencies` {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` reference to a requirement it illustrates. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.

Every defined example MUST have an `evidence/<full-example-name>.json` file whose `example` string exactly matches the current example body. A true determination MUST have at least one `{test}` reference to the example, covered by an evidence input. The reviewer MUST assess its tests under {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria` and use the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`; the no-test justification for a requirement MUST NOT establish a true example judgment. Habeas MUST apply the same missing-evidence, determination, input validation, and reference-coverage checks used for requirements. It MUST report a true determination with no test reference and changed example text with a compact line-oriented diff.

When a `{requirements-index}` chapter exists, it MUST list examples as well as requirements, identify each entry's kind, show each example's evidence state, and add one evidence detail subchapter per example. An example definition badge MUST link to its detail page. The detail page MUST link back to the example's anchored definition and to the index; references to the example MUST link to its definition. An example detail page MUST show validation findings when its evidence is missing or invalid.

An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. When present, `habeas mdbook` MUST replace it with a table of all requirements defined in rendered chapters and MUST add one evidence detail subchapter per requirement.

Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. A file-range or Rust-item input MUST show its resolved file and inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its glob and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each subsection MUST show the exact recorded text in a fenced code block. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.

An evidence detail page MUST continue to show the current requirement or example and validation findings when evidence is missing or invalid. It MUST show readable placeholders for missing rationale or inputs and expose the contents of an unreadable JSON record.

When an index exists, each requirement definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
The mdBook preprocessor MUST report an error when a generated evidence detail page would use the path of an existing book chapter.

When `output.html.git-repository-url` names a GitHub repository and `output.html.edit-url-template` uses that repository's `/edit/<branch>/{path}` form, each safely resolved source location displayed for an evidence input MUST link its repository-relative file and inclusive line range to `/blob/<branch>/<file>#L<start>-L<end>`. A source location MUST remain plain text when a safe URL cannot be derived. A generated detail page MUST use its evidence JSON file as the mdBook edit target when the file exists, or its requirement chapter when the evidence file is missing.

The requirements index MUST show each requirement's evidence state as Valid, Missing, Determination false, FIXME, or Invalid. Valid MUST mean its determination is true and its record passes the same evidence and reference coverage checks as `habeas::validate()`. A false or FIXME determination MUST have its distinct state when the record passes all other checks. The FIXME state MUST pass validation while retaining its distinct label. Malformed or stale evidence MUST remain Invalid regardless of its determination. Each detail page MUST show any validation findings.

The getting-started documentation MUST tell users with a Cargo and mdBook project to install and initialize Symposium, run `cargo add --dev habeas`, and run `cargo agents sync`, reviewing the prompt to enable Habeas's plugin. It MUST explain that the session-start hook advises the agent to run `habeas setup` when configuration is incomplete, how to refresh skills after updating Habeas, and how to preserve local edits when migrating from skills copied by older Habeas versions.

GitHub Actions MUST run `cargo test --locked --workspace` and `mdbook test` for pull requests and pushes to `main`. After those checks pass on `main`, it MUST build the book and deploy the generated `book/` directory to GitHub Pages. The book MUST set `output.html.site-url` to `/habeas-codicem/` for project-site hosting.
The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that exercises evidence
authoring against a real configured Bedrock model when AWS credentials can be
loaded. It MUST skip before reading configuration or resolving credentials when
the `CI` environment variable is present. Outside CI, it MUST fail when no
Bedrock authoring configuration exists, and MUST skip with a visible warning when
the AWS SDK cannot load credentials. Skip warnings MUST be visible under ordinary
`HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`, when set, MUST select a named authoring configuration for
the test. Otherwise the test MUST use the project's or user's selected
configuration when it selects Bedrock, falling back to the first named Bedrock
configuration in name order. Malformed configuration and invalid explicit
selections MUST fail the test. The selected profile, region, model, and options
MUST come from that configuration; credential resolution MUST use the AWS SDK.
Once credentials load, model-request and authoring failures MUST fail the test
rather than be treated as skips. The test MUST exercise an additional source read
and judgment submission using a temporary project and stdout evidence output,
without changing the checkout's evidence. It MUST retain ordinary usage history
and check the returned evidence and recorded usage. Deterministic tests MUST
verify the CI and missing-credential skip paths and the missing-configuration

A dedicated GitHub Actions workflow MUST run release-plz on pushes to `main` to create release pull requests and publish approved versions. Publishing MUST require a merged release-plz pull request. The release job MUST request an OIDC token for crates.io trusted publishing, and both jobs MUST use a GitHub token from a repository secret so release pull requests can trigger the normal pull request checks.

`habeas::validate_repository(root)` MUST return a report with the number of discovered requirements, the number of evidence files, and all validation errors for the supplied project. Ordinary invalid evidence MUST be reported in that report; an inaccessible project root MUST return an I/O error.
The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that invokes `habeas::validate()` against its own project, so its own requirements and evidence are checked recursively by `cargo test`.

For a Cargo workspace that depends on `habeas`, interactive `cargo agents sync` MUST let the user enable Habeas's plugin. Once enabled, it MUST make the skills shipped with the selected Habeas version available to configured agents. After the selected version changes, `cargo agents sync` MUST provide the skills shipped with the new version.

The enabled Habeas Symposium plugin MUST request a global Cargo installation of the `habeas` CLI and use that installation as its session-start hook command, so the CLI is available when the hook advises an agent to run `habeas setup`.

For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project depending on `habeas` MUST receive a Symposium `SessionStart` hook. The hook MUST check whether the configuration and files required by `requirements.cli.setup` are present and compatible. If not, it MUST provide nonblocking agent context saying that Habeas Codicem is not fully configured and suggesting `habeas setup`. If setup is complete or no applicable project is found, it MUST provide no setup advisory. The hook MUST NOT modify project files or run setup itself.
`habeas::validate()` MUST check the current Cargo and mdBook project and make its Cargo test fail with all validation errors when any requirement evidence is invalid.
Its failure message MUST instruct the agent to run `habeas author --all`, address
the reported gaps, and rerun tests. Validation MUST remain deterministic and MUST
The Habeas Codicem project MUST keep its mdBook Markdown in `md/` and Rust source in `src/`, and its own book MUST use the Habeas preprocessor.
The Habeas Codicem book MUST configure mdBook's Git repository link for `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem` and its page edit links for the `main` branch.

A function attestation has a Rust-item input selecting its function and a requirements input matching the definitions reviewed for it. Changing the function's raw lines or adding a definition matched by the requirements glob invalidates the attestation until the agent reviews it again. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_function_attestations`

assessed subject MUST contribute its complete fenced declaration to the
Every source containing a valid implementation, citation, or test reference to
the assessed subject MUST also contribute to that set. For a reference in a Rust
item, the contribution MUST include the complete smallest enclosing item with
its attached comments and attributes. For a reference in a Markdown requirement,
example, or terminology declaration, it MUST include that complete declaration.
For other references, it MUST include the complete containing source file.
Literal references, evidence copies, and generated output MUST remain excluded
These contribution rules MUST apply to references directly from or to the
assessed subject. Including another declaration MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that declaration's incoming or outgoing requirement and example references.

In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.

Given a requirement `foo.a.bar` and a named example `foo.a.b.bar`, `foo.*.bar` matches both, in that order. A requirements input stores both full names and their complete raw fenced declarations. Adding another matching definition invalidates the existing input. {cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs` {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`

A definition glob MUST match a complete full name. `*` MUST match zero or more characters, including dots; all other valid name characters MUST match literally. An empty glob MUST be invalid. The same glob matching rule MUST be used by requirements evidence inputs and CLI definition filters. All three MUST match against both requirements and named examples.

For every `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` reference in a project source file, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.

In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.

For every function or method covered by `references.rust_function_coverage`, repository validation MUST require exactly one attestation in `evidence/rust/<rust_file>.json`. Each such file MUST be an object with exactly `rust_file` and `functions`, where `rust_file` matches its repository-relative source path and `functions` is an array. Each attestation MUST contain exactly `rust_item`, `citations`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. Its `determination` MUST remain a boolean assessing citation coverage; the FIXME outcome applies to requirement and example judgments. Its `citations` MUST be the nonempty set of valid references owned by the function, each recorded by role and full requirement or example name. Its `inputs` MUST include one Rust-item input selecting the function and at least one requirements input; together, the requirements inputs MUST match every name in `citations`. Habeas MUST validate every input and fail for a missing, duplicate, orphaned, stale, or false attestation, a changed citation set, or an empty rationale. Each finding MUST identify the source file, current line when available, and item selector.

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to its declaration or within its body. A named example MUST cite a requirement. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count. Habeas MUST report every uncited function with its file, line, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.

Habeas MUST identify a Rust item by the pair of its repository-relative `rust_file` and a `rust_item` selector derived from a `syn` parse of that file. The selector MUST describe syntactic ancestry within the file and MUST NOT resolve Rust modules across files or use line numbers as identity. Named items MUST use kind-and-name segments such as `fn[run]` and `struct[Packet]`. Impl segments MUST distinguish inherent from trait impls using their syntactic self type and optional trait path. Otherwise identical selectors MUST have deterministic source-order disambiguators. A `use` declaration MUST have a positional selector `use#N`, where N is its one-based position among sibling `use` declarations; its import target MUST NOT form part of the selector. Other items without a suitable name MUST have a kind and positional disambiguator. Selector spelling MUST be documented and reversible when names or types contain delimiter characters.

The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.

Two sibling declarations named `run` in one file, guarded by different `#[cfg]` attributes, have selectors `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2` in source order. Their source line numbers are not part of either selector. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

A function `run` inside an inline `mod local { ... }` in `src/lib.rs` has selector `mod[local]/fn[run]`. A function defined in a separate `src/local.rs` file has a selector within that file, without reconstructing the path of a `mod local;` declaration elsewhere. A foreign function `puts` in an `extern "C"` block has selector `extern[C]/fn[puts]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
In `src/lib.rs`, `fn outer() { fn inner() {} }` gives the selectors `fn[outer]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

For a function preceded by a doc comment, an attribute, and an attached citation comment, a Rust-item input starts at the earliest attached line and ends at the function's final line. Its `text` contains those complete raw source lines. Inserting lines before them changes the displayed range without changing the input. {cite}`requirements.ci.rust_item_inputs`

For `impl Thing { fn run() {} }` on one line, `habeas add-input --for-requirement requirements.foo --rust-item src/lib.rs:1` adds separate inputs for `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`. Both contain the complete raw line. {cite}`requirements.cli.add_input_rust_item`

For consecutive sibling declarations `use alpha::A;` and `use beta::B;`, the selectors are `use#1` and `use#2`. Changing an import target leaves that declaration's positional selector the same and changes its raw evidence input. A named declaration such as `struct Packet;` instead has selector `struct[Packet]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors` {cite}`requirements.ci.rust_item_inputs`

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references.

`habeas add-input` MUST accept exactly one evidence target: `--for-requirement <full-name>`, `--for-example <full-name>`, or `--for-rust-item <rust_file> <rust_item>` identifying an explicitly declared function or method. It MUST accept exactly one input mode: `--file-range`, `--rust-item`, or `--requirements`. It MUST use the same input schema and resolution rules as validation. Repeating a selector for a target MUST refresh its existing input rather than add a duplicate; an unchanged input MUST leave the record unchanged. The command MUST report every input it adds or refreshes. It MUST create a missing target record with a pending determination. Whenever it changes a record, it MUST leave `determination` false with a nonempty rationale indicating that review is pending.
`habeas add-input --file-range <file>:<start>-<end>` MUST add or refresh one file-range input containing the current raw lines in the inclusive range. It MUST reject a missing file or invalid range.

`habeas add-input --requirements <glob>` MUST add or refresh one requirements input containing the matched full names and their concatenated raw declaration sources. It MUST report the matched names in expansion order and reject a glob that matches no requirement or named example.

`habeas add-input --rust-item <rust-file>:<line>` MUST parse the file with `syn` and add or refresh one Rust-item input for every explicit item declared on that line. An item with a declared name is declared on the line containing that name; an item without one is declared on the line containing its distinctive keyword or introducer, such as `use` or `impl`. Each input MUST store the repository-relative `rust_file`, the item's syntactic `rust_item` selector, and its complete raw source lines. The command MUST report every selected item and reject a line on which no item is declared.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents reviewing code against requirements to inspect every end-user-observable result and branch, including errors and input handling, and verify both that the code fulfills each applicable requirement and that it introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior without an agreed requirement. They MUST explain the requirement and example review criteria in {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, including test adequacy and justified absence of tests for requirements, and the three outcomes and documented-gap convention in {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Where requirements interact, agents MUST cite every applicable requirement at the relevant implementation point and explain how their texts jointly account for the behavior. A citation alone MUST NOT count as that explanation.

Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
The `habeas` CLI MUST use `clap` to define and parse its commands and options.

Given a requirement `foo.ready` and a named example `foo.case`, `habeas info 'foo.*'` displays both, and `habeas status 'foo.*' --all` lists both with their kinds and evidence states. {cite}`requirements.cli.info` {cite}`requirements.cli.status`

Habeas's bundled agent skills and any output that requests or reports a function attestation MUST explain its purpose: the configured model reviews the function and applicable requirement and example texts to judge whether the function cites every applicable requirement or named example. They MUST direct the supervising agent to run `habeas author --all` for that assessment. The model's rationale MUST explain how it identified the relevant definitions, why its requirements inputs cover them, and how the cited texts account for the function's behavior, including interactions between requirements. Matching input snapshots and a matching citation list alone MUST NOT justify a true determination. A changed function or reviewed definition set MUST be reassessed by the harness before its determination is true. {cite}`requirements.authoring.function_attestations`

`habeas info <glob>` MUST match complete requirement and named example names using `references.definition_globs`; a full name without `*` is an exact selection. It MUST print matches in full-name order as Markdown with the same kind-labeled definition, Validation findings, Rationale, and Inputs structure and evidence states as mdBook detail pages, including readable output for missing or invalid evidence. It MUST work without a requirements index directive and report an invalid glob or no matches clearly. Habeas's bundled agent guidance MUST tell agents they can use this command to inspect a requirement or named example.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST NOT offer a waiver for an uncited first-party Rust function. When a function serves only as an internal implementation detail and no existing requirement explains it, Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents to propose an explicit project requirement, such as `internal-detail`, obtain the user's agreement, cite it on the function, and run `habeas author --all` for the harness to assess its evidence. That assessment MUST account for whether the cited requirement explains the function's behavior. An internal-detail requirement MUST NOT justify an otherwise unspecified end-user-observable behavior.

`habeas mdbook supports html` MUST succeed, and a support query for another renderer MUST fail. An unknown command or invalid setup option combination MUST fail with a usage message. In particular, `habeas agents` and `habeas setup --install-skills` MUST fail with a usage message.

The `mdbook` subcommand MUST act as the mdBook preprocessor for HTML books, rendering requirement definitions and linked reference badges. This project's `book.toml` MUST configure `cargo habeas mdbook` as the `habeas` preprocessor, using a repository-local Cargo alias for `cargo run --release -p habeas --`. Consumer books MUST continue to invoke the installed `habeas mdbook` CLI directly.

The bundled requirements skill MUST direct agents adding or changing user-visible behavior in a Habeas project to draft stable requirement IDs and exact text, obtain the user's agreement, and install the agreed requirements in the mdBook before writing implementation or test code. It MUST direct agents to review substantive changes to agreed obligations with the user. The bootstrap skill MUST require user review of requirements inferred from existing code before installing them. The evidence skill MUST accept missing evidence or truthful false judgments from the harness while implementation is pending; it MUST NOT direct the supervising agent to write placeholder evidence itself.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
`habeas setup` MUST preserve existing entries in `output.html.additional-css` while adding the Habeas stylesheet at most once. It MUST report an error if `additional-css` is not an array.
When given `--path <crate-dir>` and no existing Habeas dev dependency, `habeas setup` MUST add that local crate as the dev dependency. Repeating setup MUST NOT add a duplicate Habeas dependency.

`habeas setup` MUST find an ancestor containing both `Cargo.toml` and `book.toml`, require a nonempty relative mdBook source path without parent components and a `SUMMARY.md` at that path, and report an error when these prerequisites are absent or invalid.

`habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.

`habeas status [<glob>]` MUST consider requirements and named examples whose complete full names match the glob defined by `references.definition_globs`; without a glob it MUST consider every definition. It MUST list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false or FIXME determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`. `habeas status [<glob>] --all` MUST list every matching definition with its kind and evidence state. Both forms MUST show the recorded FIXME strings for FIXME judgments and validation findings, including repository-wide Rust attestation findings, work from within a Cargo and mdBook project, and report invalid arguments or a supplied glob matching no definition clearly.

When `habeas status` or `habeas status --all` displays a Markdown table, it MUST left-align and space-pad the Definition and Evidence columns so every row, including the header and separator row, has its `|` column delimiters in the same positions. Column widths MUST be determined by the widest displayed cell in each column.

**Verdict: the citations are incomplete.** The function cites `requirements.index.detail_format`, `requirements.index.invalid_detail` and `requirements.cli.info`. At least two further requirements apply.

**How I identified the applicable set.** I read all of `render_detail_sections` in `src/index.rs`, then compared each observable branch with the supplied `*` requirements and example declarations. I also checked `requirements.cli.*` and `requirements.index.*`. Those inputs cover every candidate, so no other lookup was needed.

**What the cited requirements account for.**
- `requirements.index.detail_format` covers:
  - the evidence-state badge
  - the block-quoted definition labeled "Example" or "Requirement"
  - the Rationale section
  - the FIXME references
  - the Inputs section
- `requirements.index.invalid_detail` covers:
  - the "No rationale recorded." and "No inputs recorded." placeholders
  - the "Unreadable evidence record" JSON block
  - the Validation findings section
- `requirements.cli.info` covers the same page structure when it is printed by `habeas info`.

**What is missing.**
- `requirements.index.state` says "Each detail page MUST show any validation findings" and defines the evidence states. The function does both:
  - It renders the "Validation findings" section from `detail_evidence.errors`.
  - It renders the state badge from `detail_evidence.state.label()` and `.color()`.
  - The sibling functions `LoadedDetailEvidence::load`, `errors()`, `label()` and `color()` all cite `requirements.index.state` for the same behavior. This function, which emits that obligation, does not.
- `requirements.examples.index` says an example detail page MUST show validation findings when its evidence is missing or invalid. The function has an explicit `DefinitionKind::Example` branch that labels the page "Example", and it renders the findings for examples too. `populate`, which drives this rendering, already cites `requirements.examples.index`.

The cited requirements overlap with these two but do not replace them. `invalid_detail` does not mention the state labels, and `detail_format` does not cover the findings-on-every-detail-page or example-page rules.

Because applicable requirements are missing from the citation list, the function does not cite every applicable requirement.

It MUST compare `text` with those lines without serializing the `syn` tree, and derive the range again during validation for display and reference coverage. Moving unchanged lines because of edits earlier in the file MUST NOT invalidate the input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure, invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed lines.

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input, including one in a Rust function attestation, MUST have exactly one of four forms: a file-range input with `file`, `line_start`, `line_end`, and `text`; a Rust-item input with `rust_file`, `rust_item`, and `text`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST be repository-relative, line numbers MUST be positive integers, `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings.

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.

`habeas add-input` MUST accept exactly one evidence target: `--for-requirement <full-name>`, `--for-example <full-name>`, or `--for-rust-item <rust_file> <rust_item>` identifying an explicitly declared function or method. It MUST accept exactly one input mode: `--file-range`, `--rust-item`, or `--requirements`. It MUST use the same input schema and resolution rules as validation. Repeating a selector for a target MUST refresh its existing input rather than add a duplicate; an unchanged input MUST leave the record unchanged. The command MUST report every input it adds or refreshes. It MUST create a missing target record with a pending determination. Whenever it changes a record, it MUST leave `determination` false with a nonempty rationale indicating that review is pending.
`habeas add-input --file-range <file>:<start>-<end>` MUST add or refresh one file-range input containing the current raw lines in the inclusive range. It MUST reject a missing file or invalid range.

`habeas add-input --requirements <glob>` MUST add or refresh one requirements input containing the matched full names and their concatenated raw declaration sources. It MUST report the matched names in expansion order and reject a glob that matches no requirement or named example.

`habeas add-input --rust-item <rust-file>:<line>` MUST parse the file with `syn` and add or refresh one Rust-item input for every explicit item declared on that line. An item with a declared name is declared on the line containing that name; an item without one is declared on the line containing its distinctive keyword or introducer, such as `use` or `impl`. Each input MUST store the repository-relative `rust_file`, the item's syntactic `rust_item` selector, and its complete raw source lines. The command MUST report every selected item and reject a line on which no item is declared.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents reviewing code against requirements to inspect every end-user-observable result and branch, including errors and input handling, and verify both that the code fulfills each applicable requirement and that it introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior without an agreed requirement. They MUST explain the requirement and example review criteria in {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, including test adequacy and justified absence of tests for requirements, and the three outcomes and documented-gap convention in {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Where requirements interact, agents MUST cite every applicable requirement at the relevant implementation point and explain how their texts jointly account for the behavior. A citation alone MUST NOT count as that explanation.

Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.

The model's rationale MUST explain how it identified the relevant definitions, why its requirements inputs cover them, and how the cited texts account for the function's behavior, including interactions between requirements. Matching input snapshots and a matching citation list alone MUST NOT justify a true determination. A changed function or reviewed definition set MUST be reassessed by the harness before its determination is true. {cite}`requirements.authoring.function_attestations`

Named items MUST use kind-and-name segments such as `fn[run]` and `struct[Packet]`. Impl segments MUST distinguish inherent from trait impls using their syntactic self type and optional trait path. Otherwise identical selectors MUST have deterministic source-order disambiguators. A `use` declaration MUST have a positional selector `use#N`, where N is its one-based position among sibling `use` declarations; its import target MUST NOT form part of the selector. Other items without a suitable name MUST have a kind and positional disambiguator. Selector spelling MUST be documented and reversible when names or types contain delimiter characters.

The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.

Two sibling declarations named `run` in one file, guarded by different `#[cfg]` attributes, have selectors `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2` in source order. Their source line numbers are not part of either selector. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

A function `run` inside an inline `mod local { ... }` in `src/lib.rs` has selector `mod[local]/fn[run]`. A function defined in a separate `src/local.rs` file has a selector within that file, without reconstructing the path of a `mod local;` declaration elsewhere. A foreign function `puts` in an `extern "C"` block has selector `extern[C]/fn[puts]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
In `src/lib.rs`, `fn outer() { fn inner() {} }` gives the selectors `fn[outer]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

For a function preceded by a doc comment, an attribute, and an attached citation comment, a Rust-item input starts at the earliest attached line and ends at the function's final line. Its `text` contains those complete raw source lines. Inserting lines before them changes the displayed range without changing the input. {cite}`requirements.ci.rust_item_inputs`

For `impl Thing { fn run() {} }` on one line, `habeas add-input --for-requirement requirements.foo --rust-item src/lib.rs:1` adds separate inputs for `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`. Both contain the complete raw line. {cite}`requirements.cli.add_input_rust_item`

For consecutive sibling declarations `use alpha::A;` and `use beta::B;`, the selectors are `use#1` and `use#2`. Changing an import target leaves that declaration's positional selector the same and changes its raw evidence input. A named declaration such as `struct Packet;` instead has selector `struct[Packet]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors` {cite}`requirements.ci.rust_item_inputs`

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references.

`habeas add-input` MUST accept exactly one evidence target: `--for-requirement <full-name>`, `--for-example <full-name>`, or `--for-rust-item <rust_file> <rust_item>` identifying an explicitly declared function or method. It MUST accept exactly one input mode: `--file-range`, `--rust-item`, or `--requirements`. It MUST use the same input schema and resolution rules as validation. Repeating a selector for a target MUST refresh its existing input rather than add a duplicate; an unchanged input MUST leave the record unchanged. The command MUST report every input it adds or refreshes. It MUST create a missing target record with a pending determination. Whenever it changes a record, it MUST leave `determination` false with a nonempty rationale indicating that review is pending.
`habeas add-input --file-range <file>:<start>-<end>` MUST add or refresh one file-range input containing the current raw lines in the inclusive range. It MUST reject a missing file or invalid range.

`habeas add-input --requirements <glob>` MUST add or refresh one requirements input containing the matched full names and their concatenated raw declaration sources. It MUST report the matched names in expansion order and reject a glob that matches no requirement or named example.

`habeas add-input --rust-item <rust-file>:<line>` MUST parse the file with `syn` and add or refresh one Rust-item input for every explicit item declared on that line. An item with a declared name is declared on the line containing that name; an item without one is declared on the line containing its distinctive keyword or introducer, such as `use` or `impl`. Each input MUST store the repository-relative `rust_file`, the item's syntactic `rust_item` selector, and its complete raw source lines. The command MUST report every selected item and reject a line on which no item is declared.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents reviewing code against requirements to inspect every end-user-observable result and branch, including errors and input handling, and verify both that the code fulfills each applicable requirement and that it introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior without an agreed requirement. They MUST explain the requirement and example review criteria in {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, including test adequacy and justified absence of tests for requirements, and the three outcomes and documented-gap convention in {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Where requirements interact, agents MUST cite every applicable requirement at the relevant implementation point and explain how their texts jointly account for the behavior. A citation alone MUST NOT count as that explanation.

Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
The `habeas` CLI MUST use `clap` to define and parse its commands and options.

Given a requirement `foo.ready` and a named example `foo.case`, `habeas info 'foo.*'` displays both, and `habeas status 'foo.*' --all` lists both with their kinds and evidence states. {cite}`requirements.cli.info` {cite}`requirements.cli.status`

Habeas's bundled agent skills and any output that requests or reports a function attestation MUST explain its purpose: the configured model reviews the function and applicable requirement and example texts to judge whether the function cites every applicable requirement or named example. They MUST direct the supervising agent to run `habeas author --all` for that assessment. The model's rationale MUST explain how it identified the relevant definitions, why its requirements inputs cover them, and how the cited texts account for the function's behavior, including interactions between requirements. Matching input snapshots and a matching citation list alone MUST NOT justify a true determination. A changed function or reviewed definition set MUST be reassessed by the harness before its determination is true. {cite}`requirements.authoring.function_attestations`

`habeas info <glob>` MUST match complete requirement and named example names using `references.definition_globs`; a full name without `*` is an exact selection. It MUST print matches in full-name order as Markdown with the same kind-labeled definition, Validation findings, Rationale, and Inputs structure and evidence states as mdBook detail pages, including readable output for missing or invalid evidence. It MUST work without a requirements index directive and report an invalid glob or no matches clearly. Habeas's bundled agent guidance MUST tell agents they can use this command to inspect a requirement or named example.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST NOT offer a waiver for an uncited first-party Rust function. When a function serves only as an internal implementation detail and no existing requirement explains it, Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents to propose an explicit project requirement, such as `internal-detail`, obtain the user's agreement, cite it on the function, and run `habeas author --all` for the harness to assess its evidence. That assessment MUST account for whether the cited requirement explains the function's behavior. An internal-detail requirement MUST NOT justify an otherwise unspecified end-user-observable behavior.

`habeas mdbook supports html` MUST succeed, and a support query for another renderer MUST fail. An unknown command or invalid setup option combination MUST fail with a usage message. In particular, `habeas agents` and `habeas setup --install-skills` MUST fail with a usage message.

The `mdbook` subcommand MUST act as the mdBook preprocessor for HTML books, rendering requirement definitions and linked reference badges. This project's `book.toml` MUST configure `cargo habeas mdbook` as the `habeas` preprocessor, using a repository-local Cargo alias for `cargo run --release -p habeas --`. Consumer books MUST continue to invoke the installed `habeas mdbook` CLI directly.

The bundled requirements skill MUST direct agents adding or changing user-visible behavior in a Habeas project to draft stable requirement IDs and exact text, obtain the user's agreement, and install the agreed requirements in the mdBook before writing implementation or test code. It MUST direct agents to review substantive changes to agreed obligations with the user. The bootstrap skill MUST require user review of requirements inferred from existing code before installing them. The evidence skill MUST accept missing evidence or truthful false judgments from the harness while implementation is pending; it MUST NOT direct the supervising agent to write placeholder evidence itself.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
`habeas setup` MUST preserve existing entries in `output.html.additional-css` while adding the Habeas stylesheet at most once. It MUST report an error if `additional-css` is not an array.
When given `--path <crate-dir>` and no existing Habeas dev dependency, `habeas setup` MUST add that local crate as the dev dependency. Repeating setup MUST NOT add a duplicate Habeas dependency.

`habeas setup` MUST find an ancestor containing both `Cargo.toml` and `book.toml`, require a nonempty relative mdBook source path without parent components and a `SUMMARY.md` at that path, and report an error when these prerequisites are absent or invalid.

`habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.

`habeas status [<glob>]` MUST consider requirements and named examples whose complete full names match the glob defined by `references.definition_globs`; without a glob it MUST consider every definition. It MUST list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false or FIXME determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`. `habeas status [<glob>] --all` MUST list every matching definition with its kind and evidence state. Both forms MUST show the recorded FIXME strings for FIXME judgments and validation findings, including repository-wide Rust attestation findings, work from within a Cargo and mdBook project, and report invalid arguments or a supplied glob matching no definition clearly.

When `habeas status` or `habeas status --all` displays a Markdown table, it MUST left-align and space-pad the Definition and Evidence columns so every row, including the header and separator row, has its `|` column delimiters in the same positions. Column widths MUST be determined by the widest displayed cell in each column.

An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. When present, `habeas mdbook` MUST replace it with a table of all requirements defined in rendered chapters and MUST add one evidence detail subchapter per requirement.

Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. A file-range or Rust-item input MUST show its resolved file and inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its glob and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each subsection MUST show the exact recorded text in a fenced code block. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.

An evidence detail page MUST continue to show the current requirement or example and validation findings when evidence is missing or invalid. It MUST show readable placeholders for missing rationale or inputs and expose the contents of an unreadable JSON record.

When an index exists, each requirement definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
The mdBook preprocessor MUST report an error when a generated evidence detail page would use the path of an existing book chapter.

When `output.html.git-repository-url` names a GitHub repository and `output.html.edit-url-template` uses that repository's `/edit/<branch>/{path}` form, each safely resolved source location displayed for an evidence input MUST link its repository-relative file and inclusive line range to `/blob/<branch>/<file>#L<start>-L<end>`. A source location MUST remain plain text when a safe URL cannot be derived. A generated detail page MUST use its evidence JSON file as the mdBook edit target when the file exists, or its requirement chapter when the evidence file is missing.

The requirements index MUST show each requirement's evidence state as Valid, Missing, Determination false, FIXME, or Invalid. Valid MUST mean its determination is true and its record passes the same evidence and reference coverage checks as `habeas::validate()`. A false or FIXME determination MUST have its distinct state when the record passes all other checks. The FIXME state MUST pass validation while retaining its distinct label. Malformed or stale evidence MUST remain Invalid regardless of its determination. Each detail page MUST show any validation findings.

functions.rationale:
**Determination: false.** `populate` is missing a citation to `requirements.index.chapter`.

**How I identified the applicable set.** I read all of `IndexPlan::populate` in `src/index.rs`. I then compared its observable behaviors with every requirement and example declaration supplied through the `*` requirements input. That input covers the `requirements.cli.*`, `requirements.examples.*` and `requirements.index.*` families as well. The function does five things:
- It loads `book.toml` and the source-link configuration.
- It builds a status-table row for each detail page and renders each page.
- It chooses the evidence JSON file or the requirement chapter as each page's mdBook edit target.
- It replaces the `{requirements-index}` marker range in the index chapter with the rendered table.
- It appends one detail subchapter per definition under that chapter. If the chapter is missing, it returns an error.

**What the current citations cover.**
- `requirements.cli.shared_status_rendering` covers the `render_evidence_table` call.
- `requirements.index.source_links` covers the edit-target choice.
- `requirements.index.navigation` covers the chapter and page wiring.
- `requirements.index.state` covers the evidence-state labels in the rows.
- `requirements.examples.index` covers the example entries.

**The gap.** `requirements.index.chapter` says that `habeas mdbook` MUST replace the directive with a table of all requirements and MUST add one evidence detail subchapter per requirement. `populate` is where that happens:
- It calls `chapter.content.replace_range(range, &rows)` on the marker range.
- It pushes `BookItem::Chapter(page)` for each planned detail page.
- It returns `invalid_index("the requirements index chapter disappeared")` as its error branch.

Other functions in the same file cite `index.chapter`: `IndexPlan::find`, `marker_ranges` and `invalid_index`. `populate` itself does not, even though it carries out the chapter obligation.

**Delegated requirements.** `requirements.index.detail_format` and `requirements.index.invalid_detail` are cited on `render_detail_page`, which `populate` calls. I treated them as delegated and did not count them as missing. `requirements.index.path_conflicts` is cited in `find`, so it is also not required here.

Because `requirements.index.chapter` applies directly and is not cited, the citation set is incomplete.

Habeas MUST apply this rule to its own requirements in this chapter.

Validation MUST report a requirement or example with a missing closing fence or an empty body. Full names of `{req}` and `{example}` definitions MUST be unique across requirements, examples, and named definitions. Habeas MUST report every duplicate full name, including collisions involving named definitions, and identify both the duplicate declaration and the first declaration.

For requirement and example evidence, both `true` and `FIXME` MUST satisfy the determination check in `habeas::validate()`. A false determination MUST fail validation and be reported with its rationale. Every Rust function attestation MUST have `determination: true`; a false attestation MUST be reported with its rationale. All other evidence checks MUST still pass: FIXME MUST NOT excuse malformed, missing, or stale evidence or uncovered references. Validation MUST check the recorded outcome, schema, input freshness, and reference coverage without inference or reassessing whether a source comment adequately acknowledges a gap.

Every validation error MUST identify the failed check and give an agent enough detail to diagnose it. If the stored requirement text differs from the current chapter text, the error MUST name the requirement and show a compact line-oriented diff, with `-` for recorded lines and `+` for current lines. If recorded input text differs from the current file, the error MUST name the file and line range and show the same kind of diff. Other errors MUST state the specific missing or invalid value and the expected value when available. Diagnostics SHOULD be concise because agents are the primary readers.
Habeas MUST continue validating after an error and report all validation errors it finds in one run. Each error MUST identify the affected evidence file or requirement and explain the failure.

A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.

Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. An invalid `{req}` directive or role MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.

Every project file named directly by an evidence input or resolved from its selector MUST resolve within the project root, including when its path contains symlinks. Validation MUST report a missing or unreadable file and a path that resolves outside the project.

For a file-range input, Habeas MUST verify that `line_start` and `line_end` identify an inclusive, ordered range in `file` and that `text` exactly matches the current raw lines in that range. Habeas MUST report missing files, invalid ranges, and changed lines.

Every JSON file directly under `evidence/` MUST correspond to a declared requirement or named example. A JSON file at `evidence/rust/<rust_file>.json` MUST correspond to a first-party Rust source file containing an explicitly declared function or method. Habeas MUST report evidence JSON files in other locations under `evidence/` and Rust evidence files or entries whose source item no longer exists.
A requirement or example judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
- `true`: the sources support the subject and its testing obligations.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and source comments or tests
explicitly acknowledge those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the gaps and
their source locations in the rationale and record their issue references or
other identifying content from the inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123)`. References MAY appear elsewhere in the comment or
test; the reviewer MUST recognize explicit acknowledgments without requiring
that spelling. When no issue reference is present, the strings MUST identify the
documented gap using its source content. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in
recorded evidence inputs; a bare issue reference without an acknowledged gap
The `requirement` string in each evidence file MUST match all Markdown inside its fenced `{req}` directive, excluding leading and trailing whitespace. Habeas MUST report changed requirement text.

For a requirements input, Habeas MUST match the glob in `requirements` against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A glob matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the glob and affected definitions when available.
The reviewer MUST assess the named subject using its text, referenced requirements,
and terminology definitions. For a requirement, the reviewer MUST assess whether
the cited code implements every stated obligation and whether its tests cover the
interesting cases in the design space, including relevant boundaries and failure
cases. When there are no tests, the reviewer MUST assess whether the logic is
simple enough to need no test or a test is impractical to author, and explain that
For an example, the reviewer MUST assess whether tests exist whose setup and
assertions cover its scenario and expected outcomes. The rationale MUST identify
the relevant sources and explain the implementation and testing judgments for a
requirement, or the test coverage for an example. Referenced requirements provide
context; they MUST NOT become additional subjects to assess in full.

For a Rust-item input, Habeas MUST parse `rust_file` with `syn` and resolve `rust_item` to exactly one item. It MUST determine an inclusive range of complete raw source lines containing that item, including attached doc comments, attributes, and leading citation comments. It MUST compare `text` with those lines without serializing the `syn` tree, and derive the range again during validation for display and reference coverage. Moving unchanged lines because of edits earlier in the file MUST NOT invalidate the input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure, invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed lines.

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input, including one in a Rust function attestation, MUST have exactly one of four forms: a file-range input with `file`, `line_start`, `line_end`, and `text`; a Rust-item input with `rust_file`, `rust_item`, and `text`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST be repository-relative, line numbers MUST be positive integers, `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings.

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.

`habeas add-input` MUST accept exactly one evidence target: `--for-requirement <full-name>`, `--for-example <full-name>`, or `--for-rust-item <rust_file> <rust_item>` identifying an explicitly declared function or method. It MUST accept exactly one input mode: `--file-range`, `--rust-item`, or `--requirements`. It MUST use the same input schema and resolution rules as validation. Repeating a selector for a target MUST refresh its existing input rather than add a duplicate; an unchanged input MUST leave the record unchanged. The command MUST report every input it adds or refreshes. It MUST create a missing target record with a pending determination. Whenever it changes a record, it MUST leave `determination` false with a nonempty rationale indicating that review is pending.
`habeas add-input --file-range <file>:<start>-<end>` MUST add or refresh one file-range input containing the current raw lines in the inclusive range. It MUST reject a missing file or invalid range.

`habeas add-input --requirements <glob>` MUST add or refresh one requirements input containing the matched full names and their concatenated raw declaration sources. It MUST report the matched names in expansion order and reject a glob that matches no requirement or named example.

`habeas add-input --rust-item <rust-file>:<line>` MUST parse the file with `syn` and add or refresh one Rust-item input for every explicit item declared on that line. An item with a declared name is declared on the line containing that name; an item without one is declared on the line containing its distinctive keyword or introducer, such as `use` or `impl`. Each input MUST store the repository-relative `rust_file`, the item's syntactic `rust_item` selector, and its complete raw source lines. The command MUST report every selected item and reject a line on which no item is declared.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents reviewing code against requirements to inspect every end-user-observable result and branch, including errors and input handling, and verify both that the code fulfills each applicable requirement and that it introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior without an agreed requirement. They MUST explain the requirement and example review criteria in {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, including test adequacy and justified absence of tests for requirements, and the three outcomes and documented-gap convention in {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Where requirements interact, agents MUST cite every applicable requirement at the relevant implementation point and explain how their texts jointly account for the behavior. A citation alone MUST NOT count as that explanation.

Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
The `habeas` CLI MUST use `clap` to define and parse its commands and options.

Given a requirement `foo.ready` and a named example `foo.case`, `habeas info 'foo.*'` displays both, and `habeas status 'foo.*' --all` lists both with their kinds and evidence states. {cite}`requirements.cli.info` {cite}`requirements.cli.status`

Habeas's bundled agent skills and any output that requests or reports a function attestation MUST explain its purpose: the configured model reviews the function and applicable requirement and example texts to judge whether the function cites every applicable requirement or named example. They MUST direct the supervising agent to run `habeas author --all` for that assessment. The model's rationale MUST explain how it identified the relevant definitions, why its requirements inputs cover them, and how the cited texts account for the function's behavior, including interactions between requirements. Matching input snapshots and a matching citation list alone MUST NOT justify a true determination. A changed function or reviewed definition set MUST be reassessed by the harness before its determination is true. {cite}`requirements.authoring.function_attestations`

`habeas info <glob>` MUST match complete requirement and named example names using `references.definition_globs`; a full name without `*` is an exact selection. It MUST print matches in full-name order as Markdown with the same kind-labeled definition, Validation findings, Rationale, and Inputs structure and evidence states as mdBook detail pages, including readable output for missing or invalid evidence. It MUST work without a requirements index directive and report an invalid glob or no matches clearly. Habeas's bundled agent guidance MUST tell agents they can use this command to inspect a requirement or named example.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST NOT offer a waiver for an uncited first-party Rust function. When a function serves only as an internal implementation detail and no existing requirement explains it, Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents to propose an explicit project requirement, such as `internal-detail`, obtain the user's agreement, cite it on the function, and run `habeas author --all` for the harness to assess its evidence. That assessment MUST account for whether the cited requirement explains the function's behavior. An internal-detail requirement MUST NOT justify an otherwise unspecified end-user-observable behavior.

`habeas mdbook supports html` MUST succeed, and a support query for another renderer MUST fail. An unknown command or invalid setup option combination MUST fail with a usage message. In particular, `habeas agents` and `habeas setup --install-skills` MUST fail with a usage message.

The `mdbook` subcommand MUST act as the mdBook preprocessor for HTML books, rendering requirement definitions and linked reference badges. This project's `book.toml` MUST configure `cargo habeas mdbook` as the `habeas` preprocessor, using a repository-local Cargo alias for `cargo run --release -p habeas --`. Consumer books MUST continue to invoke the installed `habeas mdbook` CLI directly.

The bundled requirements skill MUST direct agents adding or changing user-visible behavior in a Habeas project to draft stable requirement IDs and exact text, obtain the user's agreement, and install the agreed requirements in the mdBook before writing implementation or test code. It MUST direct agents to review substantive changes to agreed obligations with the user. The bootstrap skill MUST require user review of requirements inferred from existing code before installing them. The evidence skill MUST accept missing evidence or truthful false judgments from the harness while implementation is pending; it MUST NOT direct the supervising agent to write placeholder evidence itself.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
`habeas setup` MUST preserve existing entries in `output.html.additional-css` while adding the Habeas stylesheet at most once. It MUST report an error if `additional-css` is not an array.
When given `--path <crate-dir>` and no existing Habeas dev dependency, `habeas setup` MUST add that local crate as the dev dependency. Repeating setup MUST NOT add a duplicate Habeas dependency.

`habeas setup` MUST find an ancestor containing both `Cargo.toml` and `book.toml`, require a nonempty relative mdBook source path without parent components and a `SUMMARY.md` at that path, and report an error when these prerequisites are absent or invalid.

`habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.

`habeas status [<glob>]` MUST consider requirements and named examples whose complete full names match the glob defined by `references.definition_globs`; without a glob it MUST consider every definition. It MUST list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false or FIXME determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`. `habeas status [<glob>] --all` MUST list every matching definition with its kind and evidence state. Both forms MUST show the recorded FIXME strings for FIXME judgments and validation findings, including repository-wide Rust attestation findings, work from within a Cargo and mdBook project, and report invalid arguments or a supplied glob matching no definition clearly.

When `habeas status` or `habeas status --all` displays a Markdown table, it MUST left-align and space-pad the Definition and Evidence columns so every row, including the header and separator row, has its `|` column delimiters in the same positions. Column widths MUST be determined by the widest displayed cell in each column.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
